paper.title: Learning to Play Sequential Games versus Unknown Opponents

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated sequential game vs adversarial sequence of unknown opponent types
unmapped: Two-player sequential game: learner's known reward r(x,y) in [0,1] is L_r-Lipschitz; opponent response y=b(x,theta) unknown, in RKHS with known kernel (k<=1) and norm bound B
Opponent type theta_t chosen by adaptive adversary and revealed to learner after acting, together with noisy response y_t
Learner can compute optimistic rewards for all actions (emulated full information)
settings.definition_quote: In every round t: The learner computes a randomized strategy p_t ... samples action x_t ~ p_t. The opponent observes x_t and responds by selecting y_t = b(x_t,theta_t) ... The learner observes the opponent's type theta_t and response y_t, and receives reward r(x_t, y_t).

unmapped: Bilevel objective r(x, b(x, theta_bar)) with known L_r-Lipschitz reward and unknown RKHS response b; noisy response observed
settings.definition_quote: We now consider the special case where the learner is playing against the opponent of a single known type at every round of the game, i.e., theta_t = bar theta.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated Stackelberg games with unknown followers
unmapped: Leader's action is a mixed strategy in the n_l-simplex; follower best-responds; response function in RKHS with norm bound B and L_b-Lipschitz; follower type revealed after acting
settings.definition_quote: we can map repeated Stackelberg games to our setup by letting x_t in X = Delta^{n_l} be the leader's mixed strategy at time t ... b(x_t,theta_t) = argmax_y U_{theta_t}(x_t,y)

symbols.L_r: Lipschitz constant of learner's reward r w.r.t. ||.||_1

tuning: beta_t = sigma lambda^{-1} sqrt(2 log(1/delta) + log det(I_t + K_t/lambda)) + lambda^{-1/2} B

source.label: thm:thm2
source.quote: Consider the setting with multiple opponent types from $\Theta$, and assume the learner's reward function is $L_r$-Lipschitz continuous. Then for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, the regret of \ouralg when used with $\lambda \geq 1$, ... and learning step $\eta = \sqrt{8 \log(|\mathcal{X}|)/T}$, is bounded, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, by R(T) \leq \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{2}T \log |\mathcal{X}|} + \sqrt{ \tfrac{1}{2}T\log{(\tfrac{1}{\delta})}} + 4 L_r \beta_T \sqrt{T \lambda \gamma_T}

results.notes: K = |X|. Polynomial per-round compute assumes optimistic reward max over y is efficient. Setting mapping to kernel_rkhs is approximate.

conditions: single known opponent type theta_bar every round

source.label: thm:Theorem1
source.quote: Consider the setting where the learner plays against the same opponent $\bar{\theta} \in \Theta$ in every game round, and assume the learner's reward function is $L_r$-Lipschitz continuous. Then for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, the regret of the learner when playing according to~\eqref{eq:algorithm_single_opponent} with $\beta_t$ set as in Theorem~\ref{thm:thm2} and $\lambda \geq 1$, is bounded with probability at least $1-\delta$ by R(T) \leq 4 L_r \beta_T \sqrt{T \lambda \gamma_T}

results.notes: Horizon marked anytime since algorithm does not use T.

bound.expression_latex: \sqrt{ \tfrac{1}{2} T  n_l \log \big(L_r (1 + L_b) \sqrt{n_l T}\big)} + \sqrt{T n_l } + \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{2} T \log{\big(\tfrac{1}{\delta}\big)}} + \ 4 L_r \beta_T \sqrt{T \lambda \gamma_T}

symbols.L_b: Lipschitz constant of follower's response function

tuning: StackelUCB run on uniform grid D of size (L_r(1+L_b)sqrt(n_l T))^{n_l}

source.label: cor:corollary
source.quote: Consider a repeated Stackelberg game with $n_l$ actions available to the leader. Let the leader use \ouralg with $\mathcal{D}$ from~\eqref{eq:discretization} ... the regret of the leader is bounded, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, by R(T) \leq \sqrt{ \tfrac{1}{2} T n_l \log (L_r (1 + L_b) \sqrt{n_l T})} + \sqrt{T n_l } + \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{2} T \log(1/\delta)} + 4 L_r \beta_T \sqrt{T \lambda \gamma_T}

results.notes: Paper states the approach is computationally inefficient (exponential in n_l).
